verdict.rationale: PostHog's first-party docs say funnels and paths insights are built on your existing events. PostHog AI is documented as an in-product analyst that answers plain-English questions, builds the insight and explains what it found, which supports a founder self-serving without an analyst. However, step-level drop-off analysis is only implied by the word 'funnels', and nothing shows a founder actually diagnosing activation drop-off. missing for 10: explicit documentation of per-step drop-off/conversion analysis in funnels, evidence of identifying which activation step loses users, independent or hands-on corroboration of founder self-serve funnel analysis.

support.subject: As a founder, I can answer "which activation step loses users?" myself with funnels and drop-off analysis, without an analyst

citations.quote: Build trends, funnels, retention, paths, stickiness, and lifecycle insights on the events you already send to PostHog
Ask it a question in plain English and it queries your data, builds the insight, writes the SQL, or finds the session replay – then explains what it found.
PostHog AI is an AI product analyst that lives inside PostHog.
